2025.clinched: Hungaroring feature race, 3 August 2025, one round to spare (round 9 of 10)
2025.note: Câmara sealed it in the Hungaroring feature race on 3 August 2025, converting a record-extending fifth pole of the year into a win over Mari Boya and Tuukka Taponen after a pre-race downpour forced a rolling start and two safety cars broke up the running. That left him on 156 points to Boya's 108 with a round still to run, the earliest the Formula 3 title had been settled since 2021. Four wins in a rookie season made him Trident's third champion in a row, after Gabriel Bortoleto and Leonardo Fornaroli.

2024.clinched: Monza feature race, 1 September 2024, final round
2024.note: Fornaroli won the 2024 title at the last corner of the last race. He had to finish immediately behind Gabriele Minì at Monza, started from pole, ran wide at Ascari and dropped behind both his own team-mate and his rival, then lost third to Christian Mansell at the Roggia with a lap to go, which put Minì a point ahead on the road. He went down the inside at Parabolica on the final lap to take it back. Minì was later disqualified for a technical infringement anyway. He is the first Italian to win the championship, and the first champion to do it without winning a race all season.

2023.note: Bortoleto was champion before a race was run at Monza. He arrived 38 points clear of Paul Aron and 39 clear of Josep Maria Martí with 37 available, so both rivals needed the two bonus points for pole to stay alive. Qualifying on 1 September 2023 was red-flagged three times and abandoned early, with his own Trident team-mate Oliver Goethe on provisional pole, and that settled it: he was told he was champion while standing in the pit lane. The rookie had won the first two feature races of the year, in Bahrain and Melbourne, and is the first Brazilian to take the title.

2022.clinched: Monza feature race, 11 September 2022, final round
2022.note: The closest title fight the championship has had ended in confusion. Six drivers could still win it at Monza on 11 September 2022, and the feature race was red-flagged with five laps left after a crash at Lesmo. Martins was then given a five-second track-limits penalty that dropped him from third to fifth, before an identical penalty for William Alatalo moved him back up to the fourth place he needed. He was told he was champion about 25 minutes after the red flag. He took it on 139 points to Zane Maloney's 134 and Oliver Bearman's 132, in a season where nobody won more than three races.

2021.clinched: Sochi race 1, 24 September 2021, two races to spare
2021.note: Hauger took the title on a Friday, because the first Sochi race had been brought forward a day with heavy rain forecast. He started fourth on a partly reversed grid, passed Jak Crawford on lap four and Victor Martins on lap eleven, and finished second behind Logan Sargeant, comfortably more than the six points he needed. Jack Doohan, his only rival, went backwards at the start and came home fifteenth. Hauger ended the season on 205 points to Doohan's 154, from four wins, three poles and nine podiums, and moved up to Formula 2 with Prema the following year.

2020.note: Piastri won the 2020 title by three points from the worst grid slot of any contender. Six drivers arrived at Mugello able to take it; he started eleventh with a grid penalty, dropped to tenth behind the safety car, and finished seventh after passing Sebastián Fernández on the line. Logan Sargeant, level with him on points, was out on the first lap. Théo Pourchaire climbed to third but could not catch David Beckmann in second, which is what he needed to beat Piastri on count-back. Liam Lawson won the race. Piastri finished on 164 points, the first Australian to win the championship.

2019.clinched: Sochi feature race, 28 September 2019, one race to spare (round 8 of 8)
2019.note: The first FIA Formula 3 championship went to Shwartzman at his home race. He took pole at Sochi and led the feature race on 28 September 2019 until Marcus Armstrong, his fellow Ferrari junior, went past at Turn 2 on the final lap; second was all he needed, because his only remaining rival Jehan Daruvala had made a slow start and finished fifth. He declined to risk the championship to take the win back. Three wins and six other podiums left him on 212 points to Armstrong's 158, and Prema had wrapped up the teams' title four races earlier.

2018.clinched: Yas Marina race 1, 24 November 2018, one race to spare (race 17 of 18)
2018.note: The last GP3 champion was decided at Yas Marina on 24 November 2018, where Hubert finished third in the first race. Only his ART team-mate Nikita Mazepin could still catch him, and only by winning: Mazepin took pole, ran off at Turn 17, then cut the chicane while trying to complete a pass with DRS and was given a ten-second penalty that left him fifth. Third place was Hubert's eleventh podium of a season in which he won at Paul Ricard and Silverstone, and he finished on 214 points to Mazepin's 183. He moved up to Formula 2 for 2019 and was killed at Spa-Francorchamps that August.

2017.clinched: Jerez, 8 October 2017, one round to spare (round 7 of 8)
2017.note: Russell's championship was mathematically settled at Jerez, the penultimate round of 2017: second place in the feature race, then fourth plus the fastest lap in the sprint on 8 October, left his ART team-mate Jack Aitken 50 points behind with fewer than that still available at the finale. The trophy itself was handed over at Yas Marina a month later. He won four races that year, one of them the Monza weekend that also gave ART the teams' title, and finished on 220 points, with ART locking out the top four places in the standings.

2016.clinched: Yas Marina race 1, 26 November 2016, one race to spare
2016.note: Leclerc won the 2016 title in a race he did not finish. Abu Dhabi was a three-way decider between him, his ART team-mate Alexander Albon and Trident's Antonio Fuoco; Leclerc retired after contact with Santino Ferrucci at Turn 11, but Albon, who had led the early laps, was put out by a collision with Jack Aitken at the same chicane, and that settled it. Nyck de Vries won the race. Leclerc took the championship in his rookie season, 25 points clear of Albon, with wins at Barcelona, Spielberg and Spa, and was confirmed in Formula 2 the following week.

2015.clinched: Yas Marina race 2, 29 November 2015, final round
2015.note: Ocon won one race all season and the championship by eight points. He arrived at Yas Marina six points clear of Luca Ghiotto and then lost the feature race win to a five-second penalty for running wide, which handed it to his team-mate Marvin Kirchhöfer and left him fourth, Ghiotto fifth. In the sprint race on 29 November 2015 the pair touched at the start; Ghiotto lost part of a front-wing endplate, recovered to fourth, and needed to pass Ocon in third to take the title. He could not. Thirteen further podiums from eighteen races were what decided it, and ART won the GP3 and GP2 championships in the same year.

2014.clinched: Yas Marina qualifying, 21 November 2014, final round (round 9 of 9)
2014.note: Lynn was champion before the racing started. Dean Stoneman, the only driver who could still catch him, needed pole position at Yas Marina to stay in contention; Marvin Kirchhöfer took it instead, in qualifying on 21 November 2014, and without those four points Lynn's 47-point lead could not be beaten. Lynn qualified fourth. He ended the season on 207 points from three wins, eight podiums, two poles and no retirements at all, the first British driver to win the GP3 title, and Carlin took its first teams' championship in the series.

2013.clinched: Yas Marina race 1, 2 November 2013, one race to spare (round 8 of 8)
2013.note: Kvyat took pole at Yas Marina, won the first race on 2 November 2013 and set the fastest lap in it, which settled the championship with a race still to run. It was his third consecutive feature-race win after Spa and Monza. Alexander Sims finished second and Nick Yelloly third; his own MW Arden team-mate Carlos Sainz Jr. was disqualified from ninth for causing a collision. Kvyat ended the year on 162 points to Facu Regalia's 138, having already been announced as a Toro Rosso driver for 2014 in place of Daniel Ricciardo.

2012.clinched: Monza race 2, 9 September 2012, final round (round 8 of 8)
2012.note: Evans led the standings for most of 2012 and held on by two points in the very last race. Daniel Abt had won the first Monza race to close on him and needed a strong result in the second; Tio Ellinas retook the lead late on, Abt had to settle for second, and the title stayed with Evans. Evans had taken pole for the weekend. António Félix da Costa, who earlier in the year became the first driver to win both races of a GP3 weekend, at the Hungaroring, faded out of the fight over the closing rounds.

2011.clinched: Monza race 1, 10 September 2011, one race to spare (round 8 of 8)
2011.note: Bottas won the first Monza race on 10 September 2011 to take the title with a race to spare. He had arrived five points clear of his Lotus ART team-mate James Calado, with three other drivers still mathematically alive. From fifth on the grid he was third by the first corner, second by lap seven and leading two laps later, then defended from Calado over the last three laps after a safety car, blocking him into the first chicane and running him wide at the second; Calado finished 0.378 seconds behind. It was the fourth race weekend in a row Bottas had won.

2010.note: The first GP3 champion was settled by a pole position. Gutiérrez took the last pole of the 2010 season at Monza, which put him beyond Robert Wickens's reach, and then won Saturday's race anyway, ahead of Wickens and Rio Haryanto, with the fastest lap as well. He had won at Istanbul, Valencia, Silverstone and Hockenheim earlier in the year: five wins in total, four of them in the higher-scoring Saturday races, and a 17-point margin at the end. He moved up to GP2 rather than defend the title, and was Sauber's reserve driver in 2011.
